contentBlocks.body: TypeScript ships utility types that derive new types from existing ones, so you describe a shape once and reuse it. You have met Partial<T>. The others you will reach for every week are Pick, Omit, Record, Required, and Readonly.
Pick lists what to keep; Omit lists what to drop. Prefer Pick for public API shapes: if someone adds a secret field to User later, a Pick-based type will not leak it, while an Omit-based type will.

Readonly is shallow and compile-time only. Readonly<Settings> stops settings.pageSize = 5, but nested objects stay mutable, and nothing stops mutation at runtime. Use Object.freeze if you need a runtime guarantee.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which type is { id: string; name: string } for the User interface in this lesson?

payload.explanation: Pick keeps only the listed keys. Omit with the same keys would keep email and passwordHash instead.

knowledgeItems.prompt: A teammate adds apiToken to User. Which derived type now exposes it without anyone noticing?

payload.explanation: Omit keeps every key it was not told to drop, so new fields flow through automatically. Pick is an allow-list.

payload.text: To remove every ? from a type's properties, use ____<T>.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Resolve saved settings (Partial<Settings>) into a complete Readonly<Required<Settings>>: fall back to defaults for missing or null values, clamp pageSize to 5..100, and trim locale.
